sheets.title: Patient Assessment / Management – Trauma

steps.text: Takes or verbalizes appropriate PPE precautions
steps.spokenScript: I'm putting on gloves and eye protection.

steps.text: Determines the scene/situation is safe
steps.spokenScript: Is the scene safe?

steps.text: Determines the mechanism of injury/nature of illness
steps.spokenScript: What is the mechanism of injury?

steps.text: Determines the number of patients
steps.spokenScript: How many patients do we have?

steps.text: Requests additional EMS assistance if necessary
steps.spokenScript: Based on what I see, I'm going to request additional EMS assistance.

steps.text: Considers stabilization of the spine
steps.spokenScript: Given the mechanism of injury, I'm considering spinal stabilization — I'm directing my partner to maintain manual in-line stabilization.

steps.text: Verbalizes general impression of the patient
steps.spokenScript: My general impression is an adult patient who appears to be in distress — I'm moving into my primary assessment.

steps.text: Determines responsiveness/level of consciousness
steps.spokenScript: I'm assessing level of consciousness using AVPU — the patient is alert and oriented.

steps.text: Determines chief complaint/apparent life-threats
steps.spokenScript: What seems to be the problem today?

steps.text: Airway
steps.spokenScript: I'm assessing the airway — it is open and clear.

steps.text: Breathing

substeps.text: Manages any injury which may compromise breathing/ventilation

steps.spokenScript: I'm assessing breathing — rate and quality are within normal limits, chest rise is equal and adequate.

steps.text: Circulation

substeps.text: Assess skin [either skin color, temperature or condition]
Assesses for and controls major bleeding if present
Initiates shock management [positions patient properly, conserves body heat]

steps.spokenScript: I'm checking circulation — radial pulse is present, rate and quality are within normal limits, skin is warm, dry, and pink, and I see no major external bleeding.

steps.text: Identifies patient priority and makes treatment/transport decision (based upon calculated GCS)
steps.spokenScript: Based on my calculated GCS and primary assessment findings, this patient is a high priority — I'm initiating rapid transport.

steps.text: Obtains baseline vital signs [must include BP, P and R]
steps.spokenScript: I'm obtaining a full set of baseline vital signs — blood pressure, pulse, and respirations are all within normal limits.

steps.text: Attempts to obtain SAMPLE history
steps.spokenScript: I'm going to ask you a few questions. Do you have any allergies? Are you taking any medications? Do you have any past medical history? When did you last eat or drink? And what were you doing when this started?

steps.text: Head

substeps.text: Inspects and palpates scalp and ears
Inspects mouth, nose and assesses facial area

steps.spokenScript: I'm assessing the head — I'm inspecting and palpating for deformities, contusions, abrasions, punctures, burns, tenderness, lacerations, and swelling — findings are within normal limits.

steps.text: Neck
steps.spokenScript: I'm assessing the neck — no JVD, no tracheal deviation, no tenderness or deformity noted.

steps.text: Chest
steps.spokenScript: I'm assessing the chest — equal chest rise, no deformities or crepitus, breath sounds are clear and equal bilaterally.

steps.text: Abdomen/pelvis

substeps.text: Verbalizes assessment of genitalia/perineum as needed

steps.spokenScript: I'm assessing the abdomen and pelvis — abdomen is soft and non-tender, pelvis is stable with no pain on compression.

steps.text: Lower extremities

substeps.text: Inspects, palpates and assesses motor, sensory and distal circulatory functions (1 point/leg)

steps.spokenScript: I'm assessing the lower extremities bilaterally — no deformities, distal pulses present, sensation and motor function intact.

steps.text: Upper extremities

substeps.text: Inspects, palpates and assesses motor, sensory and distal circulatory functions (1 point/arm)

steps.spokenScript: I'm assessing the upper extremities bilaterally — no deformities, radial pulses present, sensation and motor function intact.

steps.text: Posterior thorax, lumbar and buttocks

substeps.text: Inspects and palpates lumbar and buttocks areas

steps.spokenScript: I'm assessing the posterior thorax, lumbar region, and buttocks — no tenderness, deformity, or abnormal findings noted.

steps.text: Manages secondary injuries and wounds appropriately
steps.spokenScript: I'm managing all secondary injuries and wounds — applying appropriate dressings and bandages as indicated.

steps.text: Demonstrates how and when to reassess the patient
steps.spokenScript: I'll reassess this patient every five minutes given their priority status, monitoring mental status, airway, breathing, circulation, and vital signs en route.

criticalCriteria: Failure to initiate or call for transport of the patient within 10 minute time limit
Failure to take or verbalize appropriate PPE precautions
Failure to determine scene safety
Failure to assess for and provide spinal protection when indicated
Failure to voice and ultimately provide high concentration oxygen
Failure to assess/provide adequate ventilation
Failure to find or appropriately manage problems associated with airway, breathing, hemorrhage or shock
Failure to differentiate patient’s need for immediate transportation versus continued assessment/treatment at the scene
Performs other assessment before assessing/treating threats to airway, breathing and circulation
Failure to manage the patient as a competent EMT
Exhibits unacceptable affect with patient or other personnel
Uses or orders a dangerous or inappropriate intervention

steps.spokenScript: I'm assessing the affected body part and system — inspecting and palpating for any abnormalities — findings are as expected for this chief complaint.

steps.text: Provides accurate verbal report to arriving EMS unit
steps.spokenScript: Verbal report to incoming unit: we have an adult patient presenting with their chief complaint, vitals are within normal limits, interventions performed include oxygen and treatment rendered, patient is packaged and ready for transport.

sheets.title: BVM Ventilation of an Apneic Adult Patient

steps.text: Takes or verbalizes appropriate PPE precautions
steps.spokenScript: I'm putting on gloves and eye protection.

steps.text: Checks responsiveness
steps.spokenScript: I'm checking responsiveness by tapping the shoulders and shouting — the patient is unresponsive.

steps.text: Requests additional EMS assistance
steps.spokenScript: I need additional EMS assistance — calling for backup now.

steps.text: Checks breathing and pulse simultaneously
steps.examinerNote: After checking responsiveness, then checking breathing and pulse for no more than 10 seconds, examiner informs candidate, “The patient is unresponsive, apneic and has a weak pulse of 60.”
steps.spokenScript: I'm simultaneously checking for breathing and a carotid pulse for no more than ten seconds — no pulse, no breathing detected.

steps.text: Opens airway properly
steps.examinerNote: The examiner must now inform the candidate, “The mouth is full of secretions and vomitus.”
steps.spokenScript: I'm opening the airway using a head-tilt chin-lift maneuver.

steps.text: Prepares rigid suction catheter
steps.spokenScript: I'm preparing and attaching the rigid suction catheter to the suction unit.

steps.text: Turns on power to suction device or retrieves manual suction device
steps.spokenScript: I'm turning on the power to the suction device and confirming it is functional.

steps.text: Inserts rigid suction catheter without applying suction
steps.spokenScript: I'm inserting the rigid suction catheter into the mouth without applying suction.

steps.text: Suctions the mouth and oropharynx
steps.examinerNote: The examiner must now inform the candidate, “The mouth and oropharynx are clear.”
steps.spokenScript: I'm applying suction and clearing the mouth and oropharynx — airway is now clear.

steps.text: Opens the airway manually
steps.spokenScript: I'm opening the airway manually using a head-tilt chin-lift.

steps.text: Inserts oropharyngeal airway
steps.examinerNote: The examiner must now inform the candidate, “No gag reflex is present and the patient accepts the airway adjunct.”
steps.spokenScript: I'm measuring and inserting an appropriately sized oropharyngeal airway.

steps.text: Ventilates the patient immediately using a BVM device unattached to oxygen
steps.note: Award this point if candidate elects to ventilate initially with BVM attached to reservoir and oxygen so long as first ventilation is delivered within 30 seconds.
steps.examinerNote: The examiner must now inform the candidate that ventilation is being properly performed without difficulty.
steps.spokenScript: I'm ventilating the patient immediately with the BVM unattached to oxygen, delivering one breath every five to six seconds with adequate chest rise.

steps.text: Re-checks pulse for no more than 10 seconds
steps.spokenScript: I'm rechecking for a carotid pulse for no more than ten seconds — no pulse detected.

steps.text: Attaches the BVM assembly [mask, bag, reservoir] to oxygen [15 L/minute]
steps.spokenScript: I'm attaching the BVM assembly to oxygen and setting the flow rate to fifteen liters per minute.

steps.text: Ventilates the patient adequately

substeps.text: Proper volume to cause visible chest rise

steps.examinerNote: The examiner must now ask the candidate, “How would you know if you are delivering appropriate volumes with each ventilation?”
steps.spokenScript: I'm continuing to ventilate the patient adequately — good chest rise with each breath.

criticalCriteria: After suctioning the patient, failure to initiate ventilations within 30 seconds or interrupts ventilations for greater than 30 seconds at any time
Failure to take or verbalize appropriate PPE precautions
Failure to suction airway before ventilating the patient
Suctions the patient for an excessive and prolonged time
Failure to check responsiveness, then check breathing and pulse simultaneously for no more than 10 seconds
Failure to voice and ultimately provide high oxygen concentration [at least 85%]
Failure to ventilate the patient at a rate of 10 – 12/minute (1 ventilation every 5 – 6 seconds)
Failure to provide adequate volumes per breath [maximum 2 errors/minute permissible]
Insertion or use of any adjunct in a manner dangerous to the patient
Failure to manage the patient as a competent EMT
Exhibits unacceptable affect with patient or other personnel
Uses or orders a dangerous or inappropriate intervention

sheets.title: Oxygen Administration by Non-Rebreather Mask

steps.text: Takes or verbalizes appropriate PPE precautions
steps.spokenScript: I'm putting on gloves and eye protection.

steps.text: Gathers appropriate equipment
steps.spokenScript: I'm gathering the appropriate equipment including the oxygen tank, regulator, and non-rebreather mask.

steps.text: Cracks valve on the oxygen tank
steps.spokenScript: I'm cracking the valve on the oxygen tank briefly to clear any debris from the port.

steps.text: Assembles the regulator to the oxygen tank
steps.spokenScript: I'm aligning and attaching the regulator to the oxygen tank.

steps.text: Opens the oxygen tank valve
steps.spokenScript: I'm slowly opening the oxygen tank valve fully and then backing off a half turn.

steps.text: Checks oxygen tank pressure
steps.spokenScript: I'm checking the tank pressure gauge — pressure is adequate.

steps.text: Checks for leaks
steps.spokenScript: I'm listening and feeling for any leaks around the regulator connection — no leaks detected.

steps.text: Attaches non-rebreather mask to correct port of regulator
steps.spokenScript: I'm attaching the non-rebreather mask tubing to the correct port on the regulator.

steps.text: Turns on oxygen flow to prefill reservoir bag
steps.spokenScript: I'm turning on oxygen flow to prefill the reservoir bag before placing it on the patient.

steps.text: Adjusts regulator to assure oxygen flow rate of at least 10 L/minute
steps.spokenScript: I'm adjusting the flow rate to at least ten to fifteen liters per minute.

steps.text: Attaches mask to patient’s face and adjusts to fit snugly
steps.spokenScript: I'm placing the non-rebreather mask on the patient's face and adjusting it for a snug, proper fit.

criticalCriteria: Failure to take or verbalize appropriate PPE precautions

Failure to prefill the reservoir bag
Failure to adjust the oxygen flow rate to the non-rebreather mask of at lease 10 L/minute
Failure to ensure a tight mask seal to patient’s face
Failure to manage the patient as a competent EMT
Exhibits unacceptable affect with patient or other personnel
Uses or orders a dangerous or inappropriate intervention

steps.spokenScript: I'm putting on gloves and eye protection.

steps.text: Directs assistant to place/maintain head in the neutral, in-line position
steps.spokenScript: I'm directing my assistant to place and maintain the patient's head in the neutral, in-line position.

steps.text: Directs assistant to maintain manual stabilization of the head
steps.spokenScript: I'm directing my assistant to maintain manual stabilization of the head throughout this procedure.

steps.text: Reassesses motor, sensory and circulatory functions in each extremity
steps.spokenScript: I'm reassessing motor, sensory, and circulatory function in all four extremities — findings are within normal limits.

steps.text: Applies appropriately sized extrication collar
steps.spokenScript: I'm measuring and applying an appropriately sized cervical extrication collar.

steps.text: Positions the immobilization device behind the patient
steps.spokenScript: I'm positioning the short immobilization device behind the patient.

steps.text: Secures the device to the patient’s torso
steps.spokenScript: I'm securing the device to the patient's torso, fastening the torso straps.

steps.text: Evaluates torso fixation and adjusts as necessary
steps.spokenScript: I'm evaluating the torso fixation — it is secure and I'm making any necessary adjustments.

steps.text: Evaluates and pads behind the patient’s head as necessary
steps.spokenScript: I'm evaluating the space behind the patient's head and padding as necessary to maintain neutral alignment.

steps.text: Secures the patient’s head to the device
steps.spokenScript: I'm securing the patient's head to the device using the forehead and chin straps.

steps.text: Verbalizes moving the patient to a long backboard
steps.spokenScript: I'm verbalizing that we'll now rotate and move the patient to a long backboard.

steps.text: Reassesses motor, sensory and circulatory function in each extremity
steps.spokenScript: I'm reassessing motor, sensory, and circulatory function in each extremity — all remain intact.

sheets.title: Bleeding Control / Shock Management

steps.text: Takes or verbalizes appropriate PPE precautions
steps.spokenScript: I'm putting on gloves and eye protection.

steps.text: Applies direct pressure to the wound
steps.examinerNote: The examiner must now inform candidate that the wound continues to bleed.
steps.spokenScript: I'm applying firm direct pressure to the wound with a gloved hand and dressing.

steps.text: Applies tourniquet
steps.examinerNote: The examiner must now inform candidate that the patient is exhibiting signs and symptoms of hypoperfusion.
steps.spokenScript: I'm applying a tourniquet approximately two to three inches above the wound and tightening until bleeding stops — noting the time of application.

steps.text: Properly positions the patient
steps.spokenScript: I'm positioning the patient appropriately — supine with legs elevated for shock management.

steps.text: Administers high concentration oxygen
steps.spokenScript: I'm administering high-concentration oxygen via non-rebreather mask at fifteen liters per minute.

steps.text: Initiates steps to prevent heat loss from the patient
steps.spokenScript: I'm covering the patient with a blanket to prevent heat loss.

steps.text: Indicates the need for immediate transportation
steps.spokenScript: This patient requires immediate transport — I'm initiating rapid transport now.

criticalCriteria: Failure to take or verbalize appropriate PPE precautions
Failure to administer high concentration oxygen
Failure to control hemorrhage using correct procedures in a timely manner
Failure to indicate the need for immediate transportation
Failure to manage the patient as a competent EMT

Uses or orders a dangerous or inappropriate intervention

Applies direct pressure to the wound
Applies tourniquet
Properly positions the patient

sheets.title: Cardiac Arrest Management / AED

steps.text: Takes or verbalizes appropriate PPE precautions
steps.spokenScript: I'm putting on gloves and eye protection.

steps.text: Determines the scene/situation is safe
steps.spokenScript: Is the scene safe?

steps.text: Checks patient responsiveness
Direct assistant to retrieve AED
steps.spokenScript: I'm directing my partner to retrieve the AED immediately.

steps.text: Requests additional EMS assistance
steps.spokenScript: I need additional EMS assistance — calling for backup now.

steps.text: Checks breathing and pulse simultaneously
steps.examinerNote: After checking responsiveness, then checking breathing and pulse for no more than 10 seconds, examiner informs candidate, “The patient is unresponsive, apneic and pulseless.”
steps.spokenScript: I'm simultaneously checking for breathing and a carotid pulse for no more than ten seconds — no pulse, no breathing detected.

steps.text: Immediately begins chest compressions [adequate depth and rate; allows the chest to recoil completely]
steps.spokenScript: I'm beginning chest compressions at a rate of one hundred to one twenty per minute, compressing at least two inches and allowing full chest recoil.

steps.text: Performs 2 minutes of high-quality, 1-rescuer adult CPR

substeps.text: Allows the chest to recoil completely
Minimal interruptions of no more than 10 seconds throughout

steps.examinerNote: After 2 minutes (5 cycles), candidate assesses patient and second rescuer resumes compressions while candidate operates AED.
steps.spokenScript: I'm performing two minutes of high-quality single-rescuer adult CPR with a thirty-to-two compression-to-ventilation ratio.

steps.text: Turns on power to AED
steps.spokenScript: I'm turning on the power to the AED.

steps.text: Follows prompts and correctly attaches AED to patient
steps.spokenScript: I'm following the AED prompts and attaching the pads correctly — one below the right clavicle and one at the left lateral chest.

steps.text: Stops CPR and ensures all individuals are clear of the patient during rhythm analysis
steps.spokenScript: I'm stopping CPR and making sure everyone is clear — analyzing rhythm now.

steps.text: Ensures that all individuals are clear of the patient and delivers shock from AED
steps.spokenScript: I'm ensuring everyone is clear — I'm clear, you're clear, everybody's clear — delivering the shock now.

steps.text: Immediately directs rescuer to resume chest compressions
steps.spokenScript: I'm immediately directing my partner to resume chest compressions right after the shock.

criticalCriteria: Failure to take or verbalize appropriate PPE precautions
Failure to check responsiveness, then check breathing and pulse simultaneously for no more than 10 seconds
Failure to immediately begin chest compressions as soon as pulselessness is confirmed
Failure to demonstrate acceptable high-quality, 1-rescuer adult CPR
Interrupts CPR for more than 10 seconds at any point
